name: John Kerry
role: U.S. Senator from Massachusetts (1985-2013), 2004 Democratic presidential nominee, Secretary of State (2013-2017), Special Presidential Envoy for Climate (2021-2024)
summary: Kerry is a mainstream Democratic liberal: pro-choice, pro-gun-control, for higher taxes on top earners, a higher minimum wage, expanded health coverage and strong climate action, with centrist elements such as support for NAFTA, a balanced budget and a strong military. In foreign policy he is a multilateralist and alliance builder who backed limited force (Kosovo, Libya, Syria) and a two-state Israeli-Palestinian settlement. He moved from opposing nuclear power and same-sex marriage to supporting both.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Said in 2004 that health care is a right for all Americans and proposed a plan covering about 95 percent through expanded public and private coverage, not a single government payer; voted to expand CHIP and Medicaid protections.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Campaigned in 2004 to raise the minimum wage to $7 over several years, called it long overdue and a fundamental right, and voted for $7.25 in 2005 and 2007.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: 2004 platform rolled back the Bush tax cuts for incomes over $200,000; voted in 2008 to raise rates on income over $1 million and against making capital-gains and estate cuts permanent.

unions-good.rationale: Voted to restrict employer interference in union organizing (2007) and backed card-check organizing; told union halls he would fight for the American worker.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Said government should regulate on the side of citizens, not corporations; voted to regulate tobacco as a drug, backed subprime and credit-card disclosure rules and closing offshore loopholes.

cut-welfare.rationale: Voted for the 1996 welfare overhaul and block grants, but later sought to restore immigrant benefits lost under it and opposed benefit cuts generally; no statement that welfare creates dependency.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Voted for the Patriot Act and its 2006 reauthorization and a FISA warrant requirement; in 2013 defended NSA programs as stopping attacks while saying some had reached too far.

state-harmful.rationale: Defended government's role throughout his career, telling students in 2016 that democratic government, though messy, is the best way to organize life.

limit-guns.rationale: Backed the assault weapons ban, Brady background checks and closing the gun-show loophole, while saying he respects the Second Amendment and is a hunter.

empower-police-military.rationale: Championed 100,000 more COPS officers and 40,000 more active-duty troops, and voted to fund the COPS program; said nothing on more authority.

rehabilitation.rationale: Said it makes no sense to spend $50,000 a year on prison when $10,000 for early childhood could prevent it, and backed a Second Chance reentry bill to reduce recidivism.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Said in 2014 he was the first sitting Secretary of State to support same-sex marriage and recognized such marriages for visas; earlier (2004) backed civil unions and voted against DOMA.

abortion-legal.rationale: In the 2004 debates said he would not undo Roe v. Wade or criminalize a woman's choice, opposed partial-birth abortion only with life and health exceptions, and voted against abortion restrictions for years.

more-religion-public.rationale: Said faith shapes his values and urged linking good works with faith, but also kept faith out of lawmaking and voted against mandated school prayer.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Said discrimination persists and backed affirmative action ('mend it, don't end it'), minority set-asides and the NAACP anniversary resolution.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Voted for the 2007 comprehensive immigration bill, guest workers with a path to citizenship and earned legalization; as Secretary of State committed to taking more refugees.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Backed multilateral action, UN processes and the Paris and Iran agreements, but said no international institution should have a veto over U.S. security.

free-trade.rationale: Voted for NAFTA, permanent normal trade relations with China, and agreements with Peru and Oman, but against CAFTA and with fair-trade rhetoric.

nation-first.rationale: Argued American strength comes from alliances and respect ('stronger at home, respected in the world'), but kept a security veto at home.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Voted for Kosovo air strikes, backed 2011 Libya action, urged force against Syria over chemical weapons in 2013, and sought a Darfur peacekeeping force.

limit-growth.rationale: Framed environmental protection and growth as compatible: safeguard the environment and grow the economy (2003), and as envoy called the clean energy transition the greatest economic opportunity.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Spent his career on climate: signed the Paris Agreement, called climate change as dangerous as terrorism and WMD, and as envoy pressed for fossil-fuel phase-out and net zero.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Opposed nuclear spending in the 1990s but backed expansion later: said 'go for it' on fourth-generation nuclear in 2017, pushed the 2023 fusion plan, and praised the COP28 call to triple nuclear deployment in 2025.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Voted against permanent repeal of the estate tax and against raising its exemption to $5 million, keeping it at a lower threshold; no statement calling for heavy rates.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Called Howard Dean's trade policy protectionist and said cancelling NAFTA would be disastrous; wanted a fair playing field and enforcement, not tariffs.

democracy-best.rationale: In 2016 said democracy is plenty messy but, against every other alternative, the best shot there is; also in 2004 pledged to reclaim democracy.

separate-church-state.rationale: Said he honors separation of church and state and does not impose his Catholic views through law; voted against requiring school prayer.

military-superiority.rationale: Pledged to build a stronger American military, adding 40,000 troops and doubling special forces, and not to cede any veto over security.

conscription.rationale: Said in 2004 he did not support a draft and wanted to end the 'back-door draft'; backed voluntary national service.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Said the aim is preserving Israel's future as a Jewish and democratic state living in peace beside Palestine; defended its security and historic ties.

school-vouchers.rationale: Said vouchers drain resources from public schools and that nothing good about them cannot be done in public schools; voted against DC vouchers and education savings accounts.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Voted for the 2008 stimulus package and the 2009 recovery act and further recession spending, while also pledging in 2004 to halve the deficit.

force-without-un.rationale: Said he would never give any nation or international institution a veto over U.S. security; voted for Kosovo strikes without a Security Council resolution and urged Syria strikes in 2013.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Voted against limiting welfare for immigrants (1997) and in 2004 pledged to restore immigrant benefits lost in the 1996 welfare law.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Voted for the 1996 welfare overhaul (which carried work requirements) and food-stamp block-grant provisions; no separate statement of his own on a work requirement.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Voted repeatedly against Arctic refuge drilling and against the Bush energy bill, voted to remove oil and gas subsidies, said America cannot drill its way to energy independence, and as envoy urged an end to coal and oil subsidies.

night-watchman-state.rationale: His record backs a broad state: health coverage as a right, Medicare drug benefits, education funding, environmental and consumer regulation.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Consistently backed equal rights: ERA reintroduction, ENDA, DOMA vote, hate-crime and civil rights bills, and pledged to end bigotry and hatred.

separated-powers.rationale: Went to Congress for authorization on Syria in 2013, said an Attorney General must uphold the Constitution, and filibustered Alito's nomination.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Called the nation's diversity part of its strength and pledged to honor it and reject politics that divides group from group.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Called repeatedly for rebuilding and strengthening alliances; voted to enlarge NATO and defended the transatlantic alliance as Secretary of State.

death-penalty.rationale: Opposed the death penalty except for convicted terrorists, which he supported in 2004 (Osama bin Laden as an example); no later change found.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Backed sex education covering abstinence and contraception and teen-pregnancy education funding; voted against abstinence-only funding.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Defended the roughly 1 percent of the budget for aid and PEPFAR, urged investing in other countries as the Marshall Plan did, and voted against capping foreign aid.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: His December 2016 first principle: borders based on the 1967 lines with mutually agreed swaps, withdrawal from occupied territory for peace.

precautionary-principle.rationale: His book This Moment on Earth urges living by the precautionary principle other nations have adopted: first, do no harm.

collective-defense.rationale: Voted to enlarge NATO in 2002 and as Secretary of State led allied reassurance and readiness steps for Central and Eastern Europe.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Called Russia's annexation of Crimea contrary to international law and said East Jerusalem is territory occupied in 1967.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Called for progressive taxation and voted for higher top rates; no support for flat rates in his record.

refugee-return.rationale: His principle three called for an agreed solution to the Palestinian refugee issue through compensation, options for permanent homes and acknowledgment, not an unrestricted return.

no-bailouts.rationale: Voted for the 2008 TARP bank rescue and for bankruptcy changes to avoid mortgage foreclosures.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: No recorded position found: the evidence found addresses a nearby question, not this statement.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Said in 2004 all new trade deals must include labor and environmental standards and later praised TPP for raising them.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Opposed quotas but said to mend affirmative action, not end it; voted against banning affirmative-action hiring with federal funds.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Sponsored or backed bills banning breeding of big cats, invasive research on great apes and animal fighting.

notes: Answers use his own speeches, debates and Senate votes; recent clear positions win where they changed (same-sex marriage supported from his State Department years; nuclear power supported from 2017). Judgment calls: surveillance-ok (low, Patriot Act votes against his 2013 criticism), cut-welfare (0, 1996 vote versus later restoration of immigrant benefits), more-religion-public (0), jewish-state-israel (medium: he speaks of preserving a Jewish and democratic state rather than of a right), death-penalty (terrorism exception, 2004 position). His 2024 remark that the First Amendment is a major block to hammering out disinformation concerns disinformation, not hate speech, so restrict-hate-speech stays null. 1971 testimony is treated as context for Vietnam, not for current statements. Vote entries come from OnTheIssues' compilation of roll calls; Senate.gov was not opened.
